info.name: AWS Marketplace Self-service Cancellation And Billing Adjustment
info.description:
API for managing AWS Marketplace billing adjustments. For more details, refer to [official documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_Operations_AWS_Marketplace_Agreement_Service.html).

## Endpoint

[https://agreement-marketplace.us-east-1.amazonaws.com](https://agreement-marketplace.us-east-1.amazonaws.com)

## Rate Limit

2 TPS (with up to 5 invoices per batch = 10 concurrent requests)

request.description:
## [CancelAgreementCancellationRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_CancelAgreementCancellationRequest.html)

Allows sellers (proposers) to withdraw an existing agreement cancellation request that is in a pending state. Once cancelled, the cancellation request transitions to `CANCELLED` status and can no longer be approved or rejected by the buyer.

###### Note

Only cancellation requests in `PENDING_APPROVAL` status can be cancelled. A `ConflictException` is thrown if the cancellation request is in any other status.

item.description:
# Cancel an Agreement

AWS Marketplace Agreement Service API allows sellers to programmatically cancel an active [agreement](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-refunds-and-cancellations-with-api#glossary) instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller portal). When you submit a cancellation request, the buyer has **7 days** to approve or deny. If the buyer does not respond, the request is automatically approved and the agreement is canceled.

## [ListAgreementInvoiceLineItems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_ListAgreementInvoiceLineItems.html)

Allows sellers (proposers) to retrieve aggregated billing data from AWS Marketplace agreements using flexible grouping. Supports invoice-level aggregation with filtering by billing period, invoice type, and issued date.

###### Note

The `groupBy` parameter is required and supports only `INVOICE_ID` as a value. The `agreementId` parameter is required.

## [BatchCreateBillingAdjustmentRequest](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/marketplace/latest/APIReference/API_marketplace-agreements_BatchCreateBillingAdjustmentRequest.html)

Allows sellers (proposers) to submit billing adjustment requests for one or more invoices within an agreement. Each entry in the batch specifies an invoice and the adjustment amount. The operation returns successfully created adjustment request IDs and any errors for entries that failed to process.

###### Note

Each entry requires a unique `clientToken` for idempotency.

item.description:
# Issue a refund (billing adjustment)

AWS Marketplace Agreement Service API allows sellers to programmatically issue a **refund** to a buyer instead of using the [AWS Marketplace Management Portal ](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/management/)  (seller portal). In the API, a refund is represented as a **billing adjustment** against one or more invoices on an [agreement](https://catalog.workshops.aws/mpseller/en-US/manage-refunds-and-cancellations-with-api#glossary).

You submit one or more billing adjustments in a single batch request. Each adjustment targets a specific invoice and specifies the amount to refund.

item.description:
# Observe cancellation and refund events with EventBridge

AWS Marketplace emits Amazon EventBridge events when cancellation requests and billing adjustments move through their lifecycle. As the seller submitting these actions, you are the **Proposer** and you subscribe to the `- Proposer` variants of each event. This lets you react programmatically — for example, updating an internal CRM when a cancellation is approved, or alerting finance when a refund completes.

This folder shows you how to create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches all cancellation and billing adjustment events for your seller account and routes them to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group where you can inspect them.
